findings.title: No package.json, so the test is only runnable via a direct `node --test` invocation
findings.body:
`app.test.js` depends on the Node built-in test runner and is correct as written, but the tree contains no `package.json`, so there is no `test` script and no declared `"type"` field. Consequences are minor and none are defects in the reviewed code:

- CI or a contributor running `npm test` gets no test execution; the suite must be invoked as `node --test` from the repository root.
- Module resolution defaults to CommonJS absent a `"type": "module"` declaration, which is what `module.exports` / `require('./app')` need — so the current files work by default rather than by explicit declaration. If a `package.json` with `"type": "module"` is added later, both `app.js` and `app.test.js` break together.

The draft plan scopes the work to exporting the function from `app.js` and does not ask for packaging or a test harness, so this sits outside the stated deliverable and does not block approval. Recorded only so the implicit CommonJS assumption is documented if this fixture is ever built on.
